verses.text: The elder to the elect lady and her children, whom I love in truth; and not I only, but also all they that know the truth;
for the truth's sake which abides in us, and it shall be with us for ever:
Grace, mercy, peace shall be with us, from God the Father, and from Yeshua Messiah, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I rejoice greatly that I have found certain of your children walking in truth, even as we received commandment from the Father.
And now I urge you, dear lady, not as though I wrote to you a new commandment, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.
And this is love, that we should walk after His commandments. This is the commandment, even as you all heard from the beginning, that you all should walk in it.
For many deceivers are gone forth into the world, even they that confess not that Yeshua Messiah comes in the flesh. This is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Look to yourselves, that you all lose not the things which we have wrought, but that you all receive a full reward.
Whoever goes onward and abides not in the teaching of Messiah, has not God: he that abides in the teaching, the same has both the Father and the Son.
If any one comes to you, and brings not this teaching, receive him not into your house, and give him no greeting:
for he that gives him greeting partakes in his evil works.
Having many things to write to you, I would not write them with paper and ink: but I hope to come to you, and to speak face to face, that your joy may be made full.
The children of your elect sister greet you.

1: *eklektē kyria* — possibly a literal individual, but more likely (as with "your elect sister" in v13) a personification of a local congregation, an epistolary convention also seen in 1 Peter 5:13's "she that is in Babylon, elect together with you."
5: *erōtō* — "I ask/urge," the same verb used at John 4:40, 4:47.
7: an early docetic denial — that Messiah only seemed to come "in the flesh" — already answered at length in 1 John 4:2-3; the same test of true confession is applied here to a specific local situation.
10: in the ancient world a formal greeting carried real social weight — extending it functioned as public endorsement. Withholding it from a false teacher was a concrete act, not mere coldness.
